rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the Torah, the Qur'an is presented as blessing for humanity generally and especially the Arabs, who have now received conclusive truth and have no excuse for denial.
rows.anchor: It is a means of blessings for all people in general and for the Arabs in particular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is likened to rain: it revives spiritually dead humanity and restores religious guidance after alien ideas have corrupted it.
rows.anchor: has been revealed to bestow mankind with new life after its spiritual death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A governing noun is grammatically omitted before the phrase, following a linguistic convention illustrated by 5:19.
rows.anchor: Before them a governing noun ( muḍāf) is suppressed as per linguistic principles.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina means conclusive proof: the Qur'an removes the Arabs' excuses, proves its own divine origin, challenges them unanswered, and supplies reasoning as well as directives.
rows.anchor: The first of these means “a convincing and conclusive argument.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's reasoning is so strong, logical, and natural that people may stubbornly resist it but cannot deny it.
rows.anchor: that people can stubbornly react to it but they cannot deny it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadafa can mean to evade or to make others evade; he prefers the transitive sense here because rejecting God's revelations already conveys evasion, leaving this verb to mean blocking others.
rows.anchor: Those who think that it is used transitively here seem correct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched are those who reject a book that removes excuses and brings proof, guidance, and mercy, then obstruct others from accepting it.
rows.anchor: they deny it and stop others as well from accepting it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers have heard the truth from every angle yet await angels, God, or a sign of punishment instead of accepting reasoned proof.
rows.anchor: only await the appearance of angels or God before them, and if this is not possible then some sign of punishment be shown to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith professed after the promised doom appears will not benefit; acceptable faith is exercised through sight, hearing, heart, mind, and intellect.
rows.anchor: Only that faith is acceptable which is professed through the faculties of sight, hearing, heart, mind and intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once messengers and their companions have done their duty and rebels remain unmoved, they await God's verdict, through which truth becomes dominant; the aim is truth's supremacy, not opponents' destruction.
rows.anchor: The desire of destruction for opponents is not the real purpose of this waiting; it is the sentiment of the supremacy of the truth that is the real objective of this wait.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets seek spiritual purification and reform; receptive people accept it, while the spiritually dead spread disorder, so their destruction serves people's welfare. Islahi says Sūrah Nūḥ will develop this issue.
rows.anchor: Hence in their destruction lies the well-being of people. This issue will inshaAllāh be taken up in greater detail in the exegesis of Sūrah Nūḥ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path of Abraham was given to both Israelite and Ishmaelite descendants; later innovations led to polytheism among Ishmaelites and Judaism or Christianity among Israelites, until Muhammad restored the original path.
rows.anchor: the Almighty once again had it recovered through the last Prophet – Muḥammad (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to disavow those who divided God's religion, having completed his duty and leaving their judgment to God; this signals that his formal acquittal is near.
rows.anchor: the time for the Prophet’s (sws) declaration of acquittal was drawing very near.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about God later informing sectarians of their deeds entails their reward or punishment: good is rewarded tenfold, evil only in proportion, and no one is treated unjustly.
rows.anchor: Here informing them of their deeds obviously entails its consequence: reward and punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated proportion for punishment is measured by God's standard, not human judgment; the tenfold reward is a minimum and does not exclude greater blessings elsewhere.
rows.anchor: the reward of virtue that has been stated here is the minimum.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīnan qayyiman is a badal in context; qayyim and qayyim are synonymous for a straight, natural religion without deviation, describing Abraham's religion and Islam as free of later distortions.
rows.anchor: the straight and natural religion that has no deviation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah culminates in Muhammad's declaration that he follows Abraham's true religion, rejects Jewish and Christian innovations, and has no link with other deviating paths.
rows.anchor: At the end, it is declared through the tongue of Muḥammad (sws) that the real religion of Abraham (sws) is the one he is following

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk here means animal sacrifice, indicated by its placement beside prayer; 108:2 also pairs prayer with sacrifice.
rows.anchor: and this meaning is signified by its placement adjacent to the prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is compared with life and sacrifice with death: believers' whole lives and deaths belong to God, without divisions or reservations.
rows.anchor: The prayer is compared with life and animal sacrifice is compared with death.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Submission is human nature and God's command to the Prophet, who follows this path without waiting for others; those able should follow him.
rows.anchor: This means that this submission is human nature and the Prophet (sws) has been commanded by God to obey it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's submission follows from God's being Lord of everything: that sovereignty leaves no basis for associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: when God is the Lord of everything, how can he associate partners with Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is Quraysh's final warning: earlier nations were tested and discarded, and Quraysh will face the same standard; fuller details follow in Sūrah al-A‘rāf.
rows.anchor: This is the final warning sounded to the Quraysh. They are not the first nation to appear on the stage of this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unequal status and worldly resources are a test, not proof of rightness; the author begins rejecting the inference that the wealthy deniers' success proves their opponents false.
rows.anchor: The words “and exalted one of you in status above the other so that He may test you in what He has given you” are meant to dispel a misconception

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly resources test gratitude rather than demonstrate personal merit; judgment is near, when each will see the result of deeds, the ungrateful suffer, and the grateful are forgiven and shown mercy.
rows.anchor: Whatever they have is not because of their abilities; it is a test from God to see whether they express gratitude or not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persevering in prayer signifies firm adherence to Scripture and guards God's covenant; the verse encourages a small truth-preserving group among the People of the Book, later converts to the final Prophet.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, this verse sounds an encouragement to a small group among the People of the Book who adhered to the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant to hold fast to God's Book was taken from the Jews near the mountain; God's display of power and grandeur was meant to make them remember His might, but desire led them to forget.
rows.anchor: on this occasion God had made them observe His might and splendour so that they keep in mind that the God with whom they are making a promise has tremendous power.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's closing section returns to Quraysh, using the primordial covenant of all Adam's descendants about God's oneness and providence to deny them an excuse of ignorance; a messenger now reminds them.
rows.anchor: first reminded of the covenant found in human nature. It was made by with all the progeny of Adam (sws) by the Almighty regarding His oneness and providence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs had received no scripture, arguments addressed them through familiar history and evident facts of human nature and intellect; the preceding historical accounts prepared that argument.
rows.anchor: debate with them could either have been based on the history well-known to them or on the obvious facts drawn from human nature and intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding accounts of local nations and Israelites show that God sends messengers and establishes earthly judgment: rejecters are destroyed, believers succeed, and Quraysh now face this decisive phase.
rows.anchor: Whenever these messengers came, they set up His court of justice on this earth. Nations who denied their respective messengers were destroyed and those who attested to them were successful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis on gathering everyone includes the false deities and associates alongside their worshippers, who regarded them as intercessors.
rows.anchor: The emphasis sounded by the word “everyone” in the sentence “and bear in mind the day when We shall gather everyone” implies that God will gather the deities and associates together with those who worshipped them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative to stay in place omits its verb under an Arabic convention for immediate commands, focusing attention on the command; the following separation explains its purpose.
rows.anchor: when the instance is to comply to an immediate or obligatory directive, then the verb is suppressed before its locus or object

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazayyul means creating distance or alienating; other passages say idolaters are separated from their deities, who disavow their worship, humiliating worshippers who hoped for rescue.
rows.anchor: The participle ﺗﺰﻳﻴﻞmeans “to create distance” or “to alienate.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities' statement that their worshippers did not worship them is an acquittal; the source also explains the expression for witness as an oath and notes a shortened particle.
rows.anchor: The words “you would not worship us” of these deities in the verse under discussion form this acquittal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tablu means to evaluate or experience: everyone will confront their deeds, while invented deities vanish and all return to God, the real master.
rows.anchor: The verb ﺑﻶﻹ ﻳﺒﻠﻮ means “to evaluate and to experience.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā means one to whom everyone returns; calling God the true master contrasts Him with the imaginary deities.
rows.anchor: The word “ mawlā” translated as master actually means “someone to whom everyone returns.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is called the true master in contrast with the false deities, which do not exist.
rows.anchor: master” is used in contrast to their hypothetical deities, which obviously do not exist.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs acknowledged God as creator, master, and governor, but treated their deities as favored creatures and intercessors; these beliefs undermine both denial of resurrection and associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: They were able to convince God to do what they wanted. So, if they could be made happy, they could intercede for them before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Arabs acknowledged God's sole creative power and governance, they should fear attributing false things to Him and denying His attributes.
rows.anchor: if they have all these beliefs, do they not fear the wrath of God since they attribute baseless things to Him and negate all His high attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to God's acknowledged true attributes; their logical consequence is exclusive lordship, so turning elsewhere after truth is deep error, contrary to reason.
rows.anchor: The logical result of this acknowledgement should have been to accept the God Who has these attributes to be their Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs considered God creator, sustainer, giver of human reason, life and death, and governor; Islahi agrees, explaining their deities as supposed favorites delegated God's prerogatives, including sustenance and children.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, this view is correct. The Arabs never regarded their deities to be those who administered the universe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern idolaters do not differ substantially from the Arabs: both forms of polytheism are the same, despite modern efforts to label their practices monotheistic.
rows.anchor: The fact is that both are the same.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In this way” refers to the idolaters' contradiction; God's established guidance reaches those who use heart and mind, while defiant people who follow desire are led astray. The verse reassures the Prophet after he has delivered the message.
rows.anchor: He guides only those who use their faculties of heart and mind. The defiant who ignore them and become engrossed in their desires are lead away by Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that deities can rescue people at judgment: if God alone first created and will recreate them, their return and accountability are to Him alone, exposing the idolaters' inconsistent reasoning.
rows.anchor: if as per their own belief it is only God Who has created the first time and He will do it again and their own deities do not have any share in both these creations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since deities neither create nor will guide people through intellect, revelation, books, messengers, or law, they are not worthy of following; only a true guide merits obedience.
rows.anchor: Only that being is worthy of being followed who guides people to the truth or gives people the urge to follow it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prepositions used with hadā have a slight difference: one indicates guiding someone to something, while the other adds an urge toward guidance.
rows.anchor: When the latter preposition is used, it means to only guide someone to something.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahdīhim is understood as yahdītahum, with tā assimilated into dāl.
rows.anchor: As per the rule of assimilation (idghām)  تhas been transformed into

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjecture is the opposite of certainty, knowledge, and truth, so it cannot replace truth; God knows what people do.
rows.anchor: And most of them are following mere conjecture and conjecture cannot the slightest take the place of the truth.
